title: The normalized rational Tate transitions are semilinear
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an arbitrary scheme $X$. Use the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $I$ be the poset of finite intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For a topological ring $R$, write $R_X=p_X^*\underline R$, with $\underline R(S)=C(S,R)$ and pulled-back ring structure [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For $n\geq1$, give $B_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n\mathcal O_E$ the discrete topology, where $\mathcal O_E=\{a\in E:|a|\leq1\}$, and put
$$
 T_E=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\bigl((B_{E,n})_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}\mu_{\ell^n,X}\bigr),\qquad
 M_E=E_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}T_E.
$$
Here $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ is the root sheaf [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], tensor and extension of scalars are sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the limit is in $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. The action on each finite term is multiplication on the $B$ factor through the quotient $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to(B_{E,n})_X$; its transition is coefficient reduction tensored with $u\mapsto u^\ell$. The scalar-extension map $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to E_X$ is [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. Let $\alpha_E:E_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}M_E\to M_E$ be its module action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

For $E\subseteq F$, let $i_{E,F}:E_X\to F_X$ be the pulled-back coefficient inclusion [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map, det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $J_{E,F}:T_E\to T_F$ be the unique abelian-sheaf map whose $n$th projection is induced by $B_{E,n}\to B_{F,n}$ tensored with the identity on $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ [lem-route-sp-integral-twist-map-exists-unique]. Let $j_{E,F}:M_E\to M_F$ be the unique abelian-sheaf map with the localization normalization
$$
 j_{E,F}(b\otimes t)=i_{E,F}(b)\otimes J_{E,F}(t),
$$
as an equality of maps out of the sheaf tensor $E_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}T_E$ before the balanced quotient [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique]. No invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$ is assumed.

Then every $j_{E,F}$ is semilinear for $i_{E,F}$, in the following precise sense of equality of abelian-sheaf morphisms:
$$
 j_{E,F}\circ\alpha_E=\alpha_F\circ(i_{E,F}\otimes j_{E,F})
 \colon E_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}M_E\longrightarrow M_F.
$$

proof.text: Put A=E_X and write q_E:A tensor L_E -> T_E and q_F:F_X tensor L_F -> T_F for the specified extension-of-scalars projections. By [def-sfb-modobj-extension] these projections are coequalizers, and by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] tensoring with A preserves them. Thus A tensor q_E is epimorphic, so it suffices to compare the proposed semilinearity arrows after this map. The action characterization of scalar extension rewrites the first composite as alpha^{-1} followed by multiplication on the two A factors and q_E.

source.place: Rational scalar-extension construction and compatibility with finite-subfield inclusions.

proof.text: Write c:A -> F_X for the pulled-back coefficient inclusion [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map, det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], g:L_E -> L_F for the specified integral transition, and f:T_E -> T_F for the rational transition. Its normalization [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique] is q_E followed by f = (c tensor g) followed by q_F. Substitute this equality. Multiplicativity of c gives mul_A followed by c = (c tensor c) followed by mul_F. Tensor functoriality and naturality of the inverse associator now identify the result with (c tensor (c tensor g)) followed by the free F-action and q_F. The scalar-extension action characterization rewrites this as (c tensor ((c tensor g) followed by q_F)) followed by the F-action. Use the normalization again to replace the inner composite by q_E followed by f. This is exactly the other side after A tensor q_E. Cancel that epimorphism. This categorical calculation applies to every normalized g and needs neither sections of the tensor sheaf nor a separate integral semilinearity argument.

lean.statement:
theorem spRationalTwistMap_semilinear {E F : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ}
    (h : E ≤ F) :
    Mod.act (spRationalTwist X ℓ E).X ≫ spRationalTwistMap X ℓ h =
      (coefficientMap.{u} (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjMap ℓ h) X ⊗ₘ
        spRationalTwistMap X ℓ h) ≫ Mod.act (spRationalTwist X ℓ F).X
